articles.title: Melania Trump opens up about life as first lady, White House renovations and design plans, how she makes her marriage work with Donald Trump and raising son Barron
articles.summary: Melania Trump is offering a closer look at her life as America's first lady, sharing details about her responsibilities at the White House, her marriage
articles.body: Melania Trump is offering a closer look at her life as America's first lady, sharing details about her responsibilities at the White House, her marriage to President Donald Trump and her approach to raising their son, Barron Trump. The two-part Prime Video docuseries, Melania: The Series, premiered on November 20 and follows the weeks leading up to Donald Trump's January 2025 inauguration.The series serves as a follow-up to the previously released documentary Melania, giving viewers a glimpse into the former model's preparations for returning to the White House for a second time. Through conversations and behind-the-scenes moments, Melania discusses everything from managing the presidential residence to maintaining her privacy and balancing family life with public responsibilities.Melania Trump explains her responsibilities as first ladyIn the first episode, Melania speaks about the role of the first lady and the responsibilities that come with managing the White House residence. She says that people often do not realise how much of the work falls under the first lady's purview.“The role of the first lady is managing of the White House,” she explained. “And I think people don’t realize that the first lady is in charge of the residence.”Also Read| 'Look at India', 'US a country of second chances': 10 key takeaways from Trump's first presser since midterm lossShe also spoke about the importance she places on the appearance and atmosphere of the White House, including its decorations and official events. According to Melania, planning each occasion involves months of preparation, with attention given to everything from the design and decor to food and music.“I’m proud to elevate America through every detail brought to life within the White House,” she said. “Each event is carefully planned for months with the design, decor, cuisine, music, and atmosphere, all arranged with precision to showcase our nation’s beauty, strength, and grace.”She added that she wants the White House to represent the best of American culture and standards.“We preserve. We restore. We build new stuff,” she said. “The White House should be the best of the best. It represents our country.”Melania also revealed that she has plans to bring some of her own pieces back into the residence as she settles into her second stint as first lady. “I will make it a home again,” she said, recalling that her previous time there had been “very beautiful” and “very comfortable”.Her interest in architecture and interior designThe docuseries also touches upon Melania's interest in design, which she says could have shaped her career had she not entered the modelling world.When asked what she might have pursued professionally if she had not become a model, she replied, “I would continue studying architecture. I think I would do something with design.”Melania briefly attended the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia, where she studied before leaving to pursue modelling.Her comments on design come as the White House has undergone several major changes during Donald Trump's second term. These include an overhaul of the Rose Garden and the demolition of the East Wing to make way for plans for a proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom.The president also announced on November 6 that the Oval Office would be declared a national monument, saying he wanted to protect the renovations made during his administration from being altered by future presidents.“We’ve had tremendous victory in this office,” Donald said. “So we’re making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape.”Melania opens up about marriage to Donald TrumpApart from her White House responsibilities, Melania also spoke about her marriage to Donald Trump and how they maintain their relationship despite their different responsibilities and demanding schedules.According to the Associated Press, the first lady said that accepting each other as individuals has been important to their marriage.“You need to let them be who they are,” Melania said. “I let him be who he is, and he supports me and let me be who I am.”Melania and Donald began dating in New York in 1998 and married in Florida in 2005. She is the president's third wife. He was previously married to Ivana Trump, with whom he has three children, and Marla Maples, with whom he has a daughter, Tiffany.During another moment in the series, Melania suggested that her husband may not always recognise the amount of work involved in her responsibilities.“He takes the whole experience in. He’s busy with his own job, and his mind’s going nonstop,” she said. “He has so much to take care of. So maybe he doesn’t realize how much work it is.”She also made a candid observation about how much each member of her family knows about the other's daily responsibilities.“I know what my husband is doing and what my son is doing, but I don’t think they know what I’m doing,” she said.Why Melania Trump does not live in the White House full timeThe series also offers insight into how Melania manages her time between three residences. Before the inauguration, reports had suggested that she would not be living at the White House full time, and her comments in the docuseries appear to reflect that arrangement.“My home is in three cities. Each has purpose and serves varying parts of my life,” she said. “To balance this lifestyle, I’m very intentional and detail-oriented.”Apart from the White House in Washington, DC, Melania divides her time between Trump Tower in New York City and Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.She also spoke about her preference for privacy and spending time alone, explaining that she values solitude and does not feel the need to be surrounded by people constantly.“I don’t need to be all the time with people,” she said. “I’m very happy in my own company. I always was.”Melania Trump calls son Barron her priorityThe first lady also offered a glimpse into her relationship with her son, Barron Trump, describing him as her biggest priority and explaining why she believes in giving him independence.According to the Associated Press, Melania said she does not want to be overly controlling as a mother and would rather allow Barron to make his own choices and pursue what makes him happy.“I'm a very cool mom to Barron, and I remind him all the time,” she said. “He's my priority, and he will always be my priority.”She also acknowledged that growing up in the public eye has brought its own challenges for her son. Describing him as “very strong”, she said he had to grow up faster than other children because his life has not been like that of most people his age.“His life is not the same as other children,” she said.Barron, 20, is Melania's only child with Donald Trump and is studying business at New York University. The president has four other children from his previous marriages: Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump, Eric Trump and Tiffany Trump.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: No China input yet on GoPro cam used during Pahalgam attack: NIA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal Thursday said China is yet to respond to the agency's request seeking details of the supply chain that
articles.body: NEW DELHI: NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal Thursday said China is yet to respond to the agency's request seeking details of the supply chain that landed a US-manufactured GoPro camera, shipped to a Chinese commercial distributor, in the hands of Pakistani terrorists behind the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack, reports Bharti Jain.The GoPro camera was worn by the terrorists as they gunned down 26 people, including 25 tourists, in front of their families in Pahalgam. However, NIA sources said no footage was recovered from the camera, seized from the hideout of the terrorists in Dachigam after they were neutralised in July 2025.Regarding allegations by US national Mathew VanDyke - arrested in March for illegally using India as a transit point to Myanmar where he offered arms training to ultras - that he was mistreated during custody in Tihar jail, Aggarwal said VanDyke never raised this allegation during his appearance in the court here some 6-7 times.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bangladesh minister house targeted in petrol bomb attack
articles.summary: A petrol bomb was hurled at the Sylhet home of Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir early Friday.
articles.body: A petrol bomb was hurled at the Sylhet home of Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir early Friday. Hours later, Kobir told reporters in Dhaka that violence across the country amounted to "terrorist activities" by members of Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League, which is banned under anti-terror laws."It is now virtually reduced itself to a sporadic terrorist organisation. Here a petrol bomb, there they will light a fire and run away," he said, referring to arson and vandalism across Bangladesh. Sylhet Metropolitan Police deputy commissioner Md Afzal Hossain said no casualties or damage were reported. Those responsible had not yet been identified, he added.You use AI every day.
